description: A comprehensive analysis of financial transactions involving the purchase and sale of articles. This topic focuses on evaluating financial gains, losses, and discounts through foundational formulas, logical reasoning, and pattern recognition strategies.

sections.title: Fundamental Concepts
sections.description: The primary terminology required to understand any profit and loss transaction.

key_concepts.explanation: The total amount paid to purchase an article or manufacture a product. It includes all overhead expenses such as transportation, taxes, and repair costs.
The final price at which an article is sold to a customer.
The financial gain achieved when the Selling Price is strictly greater than the Cost Price.
The financial deficit incurred when the Cost Price is strictly greater than the Selling Price.

sections.title: Core Formulas
sections.description: Essential mathematical equations for calculating absolute values and percentages.

sections.title: Marked Price and Discounts
sections.description: Concepts and formulas related to retail pricing strategies and reductions.

key_concepts.explanation: The price printed on the article's tag, also known as the List Price or Tag Price. Discounts are always calculated on this value.
The reduction offered by the seller on the Marked Price to incentivize the buyer.

sections.title: Advanced Problem-Solving Strategies
sections.description: Time-saving techniques to solve complex problems without heavy calculations.

steps.title: The Base 100 Assumption
steps.detail: Whenever the Cost Price or Marked Price is unknown and the problem relies purely on percentages, assume the base value as 100. This eliminates complex algebraic fractions and simplifies sequential percentage changes.

steps.title: The Fraction (Ratio) Method
steps.detail: Convert percentage values into their fractional equivalents. For example, a 20% profit equates to 1/5. Here, the denominator (5) represents the CP, and the numerator (1) represents the Profit, establishing the SP as 6 units (5+1). Solve the problem using this ratio.

steps.title: Successive Discounts Theorem
steps.detail: If two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, do not simply add them. Use the equivalent single discount formula: [a + b - (a * b) / 100]%. For three discounts, apply the formula to the first two, then apply it again using the result and the third discount.

sections.title: High-Yield Special Cases
sections.description: Standard logical patterns and scenarios frequently encountered in competitive assessments.

cases.condition: Two articles are sold at the exact same Selling Price (SP), one at a profit of x% and the other at a loss of x%.
results: The overall transaction always results in a net loss.

cases.condition: A dishonest dealer claims to sell goods at Cost Price (CP) but uses a false weight or rigged scale.
results: The profit is generated from the stolen quantity.
Alternative formulation: Profit % = [(True Value - False Value) / False Value] * 100

cases.condition: If the Cost Price of 'a' articles equals the Selling Price of 'b' articles.
results: If the result is positive, it signifies a profit. If negative, it signifies a loss.
